preview: Bhavya Mehta shares her FTE interview experience at Morgan Stanley for the role of Technology Analyst, covering online coding, technical rounds, system design, and HR rounds.
content: Morgan Stanley : FTE Interview Experience Bhavya Mehta B.Tech CE 2019-23 Morgan Stanley visited our campus in August 2022 to hire final year students for the role of Technology Analyst and I am happy to tell you that I cracked this opportunity and am here to share my experience of the hiring process. Criteria: 1. CPI 7.5 and above 2. Branches : Computers, IT & EXTC(Electronics and Telecommunication). Rounds: 1. Online Coding Test. 2. Offline Technical Round-1. 3. Offline Technical Round-2. 4. Offline HR Round. There was a pre placement talk held before the coding round on 28th of July from 4PM-5PM where they introduced us to the Tech Stack available, projects, values and other details about Morgan Stanley. ROUND 1 (80 minutes): The test was scheduled on 28th July 2022. There were 3 sections for the coding test. a. Programming (60 minutes, 3 Questions) b. Debugging (10 minutes, 7 Questions) c. Aptitude (10 minutes, 10 Questions) a. Programming: We had to attempt three questions within a time frame of 60 minutes. The difficulty of the questions were easy, medium and hard. Q1: PS: Given an array of integers, find the minimum of numbers smaller than the element and numbers greater than the element upto ith index and return the sum of these minimums. (The question was however given in the form of a complex story, but this was the gist of it.) Difficulty: Easy Approach: Both Bruteforce (N^2) and Optimal (NLogN) worked. Q2: PS: A manufacturing firm has N outlets in a city where each outlet has been identified by a unique ID ranging from Oto (N-1). Each outlet receives the order from customers. Each outlet has P inventories, where the positive inventory P denotes that P units are in stock and negative inventory -P denotes that the P units are out of stock. The firm has decided to better serve its customers by providing the out of stock inventory of one outlet from the other outlet where the inventories are in stock. The stock that will be shifted from the outlet will be replenished by the firm's warehouse. However, only one outlet can be replenished at a single time. If there are multiple outlets that can nearly fulfill the requirements of the other outlets and the out of stock units are same as number of surplus units after replenishment then output the pair of outlets which will still require stock replenishment. Write an algorithm to find the pair of units where the first outlet is out of stock but can be replenished from the second outlet. If the value of units becomes surplus after stock replenishment and the value of units out of stock left after stock replenishment is same then output the pair which is still needs to be replenished. Difficulty: Medium Approach: So basically we had to sort the array and find the minimum absolute difference between positive & negative elements. If there is a tie then select the one which has a negative difference. Input: 6 18 -28 -50 -60 58 30 Output: 60 58 Explanation: The pair of outlets whose out of stock units can be nearly replenished from the other outlet are {outlet1,outlet5} i.e. (-28, 30) and (outlet3, outlet4) i.e. (-60, 58). But according to Note, we have to select that pair which still needs stock replenishment because we can't afford to leave the two units surplus (i.e. -28+30= 2) for the outlet because of limited stock. So, the output is (-60, 58) Q3: PS: Given the nodes and the edges between nodes of a tree, write a function to print the boundary order traversal. (The problem was again as a long story and getting to the point that boundary traversal is to be done took some time) Difficulty: Hard Approach: A1: Using the edges create a tree and perform boundary order traversal on it. But this method was time consuming as it included recursion for tree creation and hence did not pass all the test cases. Also implementing the code for tree creation took a lot of time. A2: Create an adjacency list and perform traversal using it. I implemented the first approach but due to time constraints I was not able to solve it completely. The second approach was suggested by my friend. b. Debugging We were asked to choose our preferred programming language and the 7 Questions popped up. We were given code snippets and had to make corrections for the code to run properly. Three questions were based upon compilation and syntax errors. Two of them were code completion ( Quick sort and find value of x^y given x & y) One of them was based on OOPS ( Accessing private variables) One was based on recursion. c. Aptitude There were a total of 10 Questions based on probability,charts, statistics and basic math. I was able to solve the first two coding Qs completely and the third with partial test cases. The Debugging and Aptitude Qs were pretty easy and I could solve all of them except for one in the debugging part. Just a day before the offline interviews on 1st August, we had the list of selected candidates out which had a total 17 and I was one of them. ROUND 2 (1hour 30minutes): Offline interviews were scheduled on 1st August, 2022 starting from 9:30 AM. I had my interview at 3:15 PM. They asked Questions on a lot of things including my resume. Projects, DSA, OOPS, OS and DBMS. 1. Introduce yourself. 2. What is the difference between C and C++ 3. What makes C++ special ( 4 pillars of OOPS) 4. I was then asked to explain each one of them in detail. 5. The interviewer then asked whether I drive cars or not. I replied YES and he asked me to explain the concept of OOPs in cars. ( I explained it using the example of clutch as polymorphism, gear box as abstraction, steering as encapsulation etc) He was quite satisfied with my answer. 6. He then asked types of inheritance and asked to explain it using the example of our college as to where and how inheritance occurs. 7. I was also questioned on virtual functions and abstract keywords. 8. He also hoped I would be aware of vtable and vpointer. 9. He then moved to my resume and asked me about my internship work at Butterflies. 10. As I had mentioned Codechef and Leetcode in my introduction, he then asked me a Hard Question on graphs. The question as follows: Given three arrays of recipes, constituents and ingredients return an boolean array which shows if that recipe can be made or not. So to make a sandwich I need bread and cucumber. To prepare bread I need Flour and Yeast and so on. Recipes:[ Bread, Sandwich] Constitutes:[ [Flour, Yeast], [Bread, Cucumber]] Ingredients:[ Flour, Yeast, Cucumber] Having this understood, I explained that this can be solved using topological sort wherein each node represents an entity and edges are from constituents to recipe. If there exists a valid topo sort for the graph then the recipes can be made. So for my case this is the graph that can be made. Upon toposort we get the sequence as F, Y, B, C, S; Now using this sequence we check if for each recipe, has its ingredients come before its index returns true for them.He was okay with this approach and asked me to code it on paper. While coding he asked me questions like what is an adjacency list, why not a matrix, how do you show directions in a graph etc. I explained the topo sort using DFS and stack. 11. Having mentioned stack he then moved on to it. Asked about working on a stack. 12. What is the difference between stack and queues? 13. How do you implement a stack using two queues? 14. Having answered these he then moved back to the original question where he pinpointed in my code that there may exist an issue of loops and we would get an incorrect topo sort. Building upon this I explained that we can either go for a BFS approach ( Khan’s algorithm) or have checks for cycles. He asked me to proceed with the latter. 15. I then explained the algorithm for cycle detection in a directed graph using DFS. After explaining it he then asked me if I knew any other methods for detecting cycles. I had to then explain the BFS approach as well. 16. For all the algorithms that I had mentioned he asked to explain the time and space complexities. 17. There was a thorough discussion between me and the interviewers on graphs which took almost 20-25 minutes. 18. The interview again came back to my resume and asked me to explain all of my projects. They were intimidated by one of my project on A* , minimax and Genetic algorithms, so I had to explain that also. 19. Moving on they switched to frontend development. They had a rapid fire round with lots of questions on DOM management and other HTML basics. 20. Why do we need doctype? Will HTML run without this line? 21. Does HTML need a compiler? Is HTML a programming language? 22. Is javascript a programming language? How does it compile? 23. What does ++ stand for in C++? And so forth. (I was able to answer some properly while I had no idea for some) 24. Moving on to OS where I was questioned about kernels (user level and OS level), threading and multiprocessing. 25. He also asked about different scheduling algorithms and deadlocks. 26. To end the interview, they moved onto DBMS and asked me to write some queries like find 3rd highest of something and some on joins. 27. Later on I was asked about normalization forms and its need. 28. Lastly, do you have any questions for us? (Always ask some) With this round ending at 5PM, the list was out and 8 candidates were selected for further rounds. ROUND 3 (40 minutes): This round started at 5:15 where I was the first one being called. The questions asked were as follows: 1. Introduce yourself 2. As I had interned at JPMC, he asked to explain my entire work in detail. I was asked questions on tech stack, deployment, java design patterns and much more. 3. As my project involved encryption he moved to encryption algorithms where I explained to him about RSA, AES, DES and the concept of public-private key. 4. He moved to Java design patterns and asked me explain them ( I had very preliminary knowledge about so just mentioned about Builder and Abstract ones) 5. I was then asked If I watch cricket ( Yes obviously) and following that I was asked to present a high level design for cricbuzz with real time score updates ( I explained some basic terminologies but he wasn't satisfied) 6. I was then redirected to explaining the low level design of it where I had to code classes and methods for teams and score updations. 7. The interviewer then asked some math and probability questions 8. Post this I was cross questioned on one of my internships where I worked on trading algorithms using multi threading. 9. I was asked to explain about fork , join, pid and some OS details 10. Post this they asked if I had any questions for them. I did perform okayish in the system design part, but they were balanced out with other parts of my interview. Following this round all 8 candidates were called for the HR on a rolling basis and I was the first one for the HR/ Managerial round. ROUND 4 (20 minutes): Basically in this round, you have to talk about yourself and your experiences. Make sure you are confident and you have prepared answers to these questions well in advance. Trust me it helps. I was asked common Technical and HR questions. The interviewer asked me the following questions: 1. Tell me about yourself. 2. I was asked about my Internship Experience, the Pros, and Cons of a Virtual Internship. 3. He then asked me to elaborate on all of my projects. ( Not much in the technical essence) 4. As my resume had many hackathon participations and wins, he asked me how I managed my academics and college with hackathons? The interviewer was frank and asked me if I used to bunk the classes for attending competitions and hackathons. 5. How did you manage conflicts while being in a team? 6. What was the toughest task assigned to you? 7. As it was more of an interactive session I also asked him Qs on tech stacks and why a Computer Engineer should work in a bank. 8. He then moved onto his own life journey as to how he has learnt so much and how MS makes him evolve everyday. 9. There were more HR Questions but can be easily found online. My HR round ended at 8pm. I was happy with my performance but at the same time tensed for the results. The interviewers were good and helped me when I was stuck. Finally, the next day, at 9AM, the results were announced. 4 out of 8 students were given the offers and I was happy to be one of them. It was a tiring day whose end turned out to be a memorable one. SOME TIPS: 1. NEVER FORGET TO RESEARCH ABOUT THE COMPANY. The interviewer would most probably ask you about the company’s mission, vision, values or what it does. 2. DO NOT LIE IN YOUR RESUME, they may ask questions from it and you may go blank. 3. Don’t forget to prepare yourself for behavioral questions. Sometimes, we focus a lot on technical questions and completely ignore behavioral questions. 4. Have a look at some interview experiences before the interview. You can find a lot of interview experiences on Geeks for Geeks. This really helps in the interview. 5. Don’t lose hope, even though you feel that you could not perform the way you wanted to. Stay calm and composed during the interview. 6. Remember that your body language says as much about you as your answers to the questions. Resources for preparation for any company: 1. Interview Prep Resources (GitHub) 2. Practice DSA from Leetcode, InterviewBit and Geeks for Geeks. 3. Company Interview Corner (GeeksForGeeks) 4. Prepare According to a particular company. What I mean by this is that some companies are more focused towards asking questions on DBMS, whereas some companies may ask system design. It also depends on the interviewer but do have a look at company archives to get an idea. 5. Practice SQL queries from interviewbit and other sites. 6. Revise OOPS concepts and be aware of the diamond problem. You should at least be familiar with the following Concepts. SQL : ● Basic DDL,DML queries. ● Joins, Unions,constraints. ● Aggregate functions,Group by, order by. ● LIKE, BETWEEN and IN operator ● Transactions, Concurrency Control problems and Protocols. ● Indexing, Normalization, SQL injection. CN : ● OSI Model, TCP-IP Model. ● Types of Topologies, connecting devices and end devices. ● Some important protocols. OS : ● Scheduling algorithms, Page replacement algorithms,Disk Scheduling algorithms. ● Deadlock, semaphore, mutex,Threading, Segmentation. ● Bankers algorithm, Producer-Consumer problem. System design. ● Saumyajit Bhattacharya & Gaurav Sen (Youtube) PS: In case you have any doubts or anything to ask for, please feel free to drop me an email or contact me on my cell.
